relevance_note: Single-patient case report in which whole-exome sequencing "identified the heterozygous variant c.1420A>G (p.Thr474Ala) in exon7 of the TNFAIP3 gene" in a boy with chronic ITP and vitiligo; the authors classify it as a VUS.
method_note: Read the whole paper manually; output assembled with a short Python script from hand-chosen values and spans, then every span checked verbatim against the Markdown. One person only (unnamed; label 'patient'). Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) bleeding: the case presentation reports 'a history of mild epistaxis' and 'multiple hospitalizations due to recurrent epistaxis and ecchymosis', but the Discussion says 'Our patient did not report any history of bleeding in the past' and 'no bleeding was observed in our patient'; both observed and excluded rows emitted (no checklist item affected). (2) Abstract says he 'did not respond to rituximab or eltrombopag', whereas the case text reports a rise to 457 x 10^9/L on eltrombopag 75 mg followed by loss of response. (3) Gene printed once as 'TNFAJP3' (typo) in the Discussion; elsewhere TNFAIP3. (4) 'A 12-year-old-boy presented for the first time in April 2017' (first presentation to the authors' center) vs 'nine years old at the time of the first presentation'; age 9 recorded as onset (first presentation) and as age at ITP diagnosis; age at last evaluation not stated (follow-up runs to at least late 2019) so left not reported; age at genetic diagnosis not stated. Judgement calls: 'Our case did not report any such features' follows the list of Zhou et al. features (ulcers, polyarthritis, skin rash, uveitis, fever, hemolytic anemia) but its referent is ambiguous (may mean only the Behcet-type ulcer features), so it was NOT used to exclude fever, rash, polyarthritis or hemolytic anemia. Uveitis checklist item set to excluded from the ophthalmology consultation with 'no significant findings'; arthritis/arthralgia excluded from 'no history of ... joint involvement' plus normal musculoskeletal examination; lymphoproliferation/lymphadenopathy excluded from 'no organomegaly or lymphadenopathy' plus normal double-negative T cells; skin lesions checklist item set to observed on the basis of vitiligo (depigmented patches), which is not one of the listed examples. Variant type 'missense' mapped from the authors' wording 'leads to an amino acid exchange'. In silico predictions ('10 of 16 bioinformatics in silico programs predict a pathogenic') are not a functional assay, so functional evidence is not reported. No genome build printed for chr6:138200002. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients left null: the paper does not mention any earlier report of this patient.
